what: The LATIN-SCRIPT half of the G5c native-speaker review -- every Latin-script name in the Grades 6-12 page-truth corpus that lint_lp.js's TRANSLIT_PROPHET_RE matches, as decided by the reviewer of record. This file IS the clearance brief §4c requires; it is not a heuristic and nothing else in this repo may decide which Mohammad is which.
status_note: 134 of 134 rows decided by the reviewer of record (15 prophet, 119 person, 0 undecided). An undecided row appears in NEITHER list and stays refused. FAIL-CLOSED, ALWAYS -- an unreviewed name is not a cleared name.
reviewer_role: native-speaker reviewer of record for gate G5c, named on the Grades 6-12 curriculum workbook Change Log as row H-0001

polarity.prophet: the Prophet -- the salutation is required and the gate keeps demanding it
polarity.person: an ordinary named person -- no salutation, and the gate must stop demanding one

polarity_note: The sheet asked one question on every row -- 'Is this phrase the Prophet ﷺ?' -- so Y means prophet and N means person. The reviewer answered in that polarity and the two lists below are a direct transcription of her column.
derived_how: probes/build-cleared-names-en.py -- a transcription of the reviewer's Y/N column only. The recommendation column in the same sheet is NOT read. A cell that does not begin with a bare Y or N is treated as undecided and clears nothing.
matching: The gate matches on the WORD SEQUENCE, not the byte string: each word is compared with its edge punctuation trimmed and its case folded, because the books print 'MOHAMMAD ALI JINNAH' in a heading and 'Mohammad Ali Jinnah' in the prose. The longest decided phrase present rules, and on equal length the blocking mark wins.

reviewer_notes.Muhammad: Reviewer, on the bare token: 'mised, Sultan is normal person but Fatima hadith needs the salutation'. She ruled the token MIXED -- it carries both Muhammad al-Fatih and the Fatima hadith -- and marked it PROPHET to fail safe. The bare token therefore keeps demanding a salutation; the longer decided phrases around it (e.g. 'Muhammad Ali Jinnah') are what clear the ordinary people, which is exactly what longest-phrase-wins is for.
reviewer_notes.Rasul: Reviewer: 'it should be after Rasul'. A PLACEMENT instruction for the title 'Khalifa tu Rasul' -- the salutation belongs after Rasul, not mid-title. The mark is PROPHET; where the stamp renders is a separate question this file does not decide.
reviewer_notes.Hazrat Muhammad PBUH / Hazrat Muhammad S: Both marked PROPHET, correctly -- these denote the Prophet. Note the consequence: the gate's honorific test recognises only the single glyph and the Arabic form, so these correctly-saluted lines stay refused until the Latin honorific forms are recognised. That defect is bd-b7txa and is explicitly OUT of this file's scope.
